subject.title: Dashboard /compact silently wipes context once Claude CLI session is over the 1M cap

question: What should OpenClaw guarantee when a Dashboard user requests `/compact` for a Claude CLI native session that is already past the native 1M-token cap?
rationale: Current source deliberately defers non-harness Claude CLI compaction to Claude Code, while the reported user harm requires choosing between fail-loud recovery UX, native transcript recovery, or accepting provider-owned behavior.

options.title: Fail Loud With Recovery Guidance
options.body: Keep deferring native Claude CLI compaction for now, but detect the over-cap/no-real-conversation case and show export or manual-prune guidance without rotating or accepting an empty checkpoint.

options.title: Build Native/Fallback Recovery
options.body: Implement a Claude CLI transcript reader and fallback summarization path that can compact or reseed an over-cap native transcript inside OpenClaw.

options.title: Accept Provider-Owned Deferral
options.body: Document that Claude CLI over-cap recovery is outside OpenClaw and close only after maintainers accept that Dashboard `/compact` may report no recovery for those sessions.

recommendation.title: Fail Loud With Recovery Guidance
recommendation.body: Keep deferring native Claude CLI compaction for now, but detect the over-cap/no-real-conversation case and show export or manual-prune guidance without rotating or accepting an empty checkpoint.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and followed up on the native CLI compaction ownership contract that this decision would refine.
